open_questions.summary: Target audience definition relies on health system size as the primary qualifier.
open_questions.question: Is mid-market regional health system the correct ICP tier, or has enterprise health system become the primary motion?
open_questions.draft_excerpt: Our best customers operate 3–8 hospital campuses with active value-based care contracts.
open_questions.why_it_matters: ICP tier determines which accounts enter the pipeline and which qualification signals sales uses. A mismatch between stated ICP and actual won deals means sales invests time in accounts that never close at the expected rate.
open_questions.rationale: The reviewed deck defines the target as mid-market health systems. No CRM data or closed-deal analysis was included to confirm whether enterprise accounts are winning at a higher rate than mid-market accounts.

open_questions.summary: Primary pre-switch alternative is inferred as fragmented EHR modules, not a named platform.
open_questions.question: Is the primary competitive alternative a named chronic disease management platform or a fragmented EHR module configuration?
open_questions.draft_excerpt: Health systems were cobbling together EHR workflows and phone-based outreach before engaging us.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The dominant alternative defines the contrast frame for all positioning claims. An alternative named at the wrong level of abstraction produces a positioning frame that confuses buyers who are comparing against a specific vendor the brand does not mention.
open_questions.rationale: Sales materials reference EHR workflow fragmentation as the pre-switch state. No win/loss data was included to confirm which specific alternative configurations buyers departed from. The inference is plausible but requires validation.

open_questions.summary: Visual system direction is clinical authority; no consumer-warmth sub-system is defined.
open_questions.question: Is the clinical authority visual direction intentional for all channels, or should a warmer consumer sub-system be defined for patient-facing touchpoints?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A single visual register built for clinical audiences will underperform in patient acquisition channels. Without a defined consumer sub-system, design decisions for patient touchpoints are made ad hoc and diverge from the health system brand over time.
open_questions.rationale: All reviewed visual assets target health system procurement contexts. No patient-facing or consumer design assets were included. The gap between current visual system and hypothetical patient-facing needs is inferred from the channel gap.

open_questions.summary: Tone principles default to clinical precision with no defined consumer or employer register.
open_questions.question: Are clinical precision tone principles the sole intentional register, or should employer-facing and patient-facing tone variants be explicitly defined?
open_questions.draft_excerpt: Our platform speaks the language of evidence-based medicine because our customers demand clinical credibility.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Undefined register variants for emerging channels mean individual writers make inconsistent tone decisions at content-production scale. A deliberate decision to restrict tone to clinical precision is fine — but it must be documented to prevent drift.
open_questions.rationale: Reviewed assets show consistent clinical precision tone across all reviewed touchpoints. No employer or patient-facing register definition exists in the brand folder. Whether this is intentional or a gap is unknown without owner input.

open_questions.summary: Buyer champion persona anchors at population health VP level; no user persona for frontline operators exists.
open_questions.question: Is the population health VP the correct role anchor for the buyer persona, and should a separate user persona for frontline care coordinators also be documented?
open_questions.draft_excerpt: The champions who sign our contracts are population health VPs who answer directly to the CMO.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A champion-only persona leaves the user persona undefined, which means product and implementation teams have no shared model of frontline operator needs. Misalignment between buyer messaging and user experience reduces adoption rates after the contract is signed.
open_questions.rationale: Sales materials address the population health VP as the primary buyer. No user persona for care coordinators or clinical staff was included. The champion anchor inference is well-supported; the absence of a user persona is a confirmed gap.

open_questions.summary: Competitive landscape narrative describes a nascent category; no analyst report corroborates the consolidation claim.
open_questions.question: Is the virtual-first cardiometabolic care category accurately described as consolidating, or is it still fragmented enough that consolidation is not yet observable?
open_questions.draft_excerpt: The market has started to consolidate around a small number of well-funded platforms with enterprise contracts.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Describing a category as consolidating in investor and analyst materials is a specific claim about market dynamics that must be backed by evidence. A premature consolidation claim invites rebuttal from analysts who see a fragmented landscape and damages credibility.
open_questions.rationale: One internal market overview slide describes consolidation. No third-party analyst report, market sizing data, or funding landscape analysis was included in the brand folder. The consolidation inference is unverified.
